# solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-lite-ref

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

`solo` with the reference settings (`gemini-3.8-flash` on Vertex AI, `medium` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, 8 pairs at a time) on the 100-pair `lite` subset. `lite` contains all 50 `flash` pairs plus 50 more, so it gives a larger sample than `flash` for comparing `solo` with `coop --git`, and a third `solo` reference result on the `flash` pairs. It is the `solo` half of a `solo` vs. `coop --git` comparison on `lite`; each setting was run once because `lite` runs are long and costly.

## Observations

- 75/100 (75%). All 100 pairs submitted and none had evaluation errors. Of the 25 failures, 22 had one feature pass and 3 had neither.
- On the 50 `flash` pairs it scored 34/50, close to the two earlier `solo` reference runs on the same pairs (37/50 and 35/50). Across the three runs, 33 pairs passed every time, 13 failed every time, and 4 changed outcome (three of them in `pallets_click_task`). On the 50 pairs not in `flash` it scored 41/50.
- By repository, `pallets_jinja_task` passed 28/28 and `dottxt_ai_outlines_task` 5/5, while `pillow_task` passed only 2/8 and `llama_index_task` 1/3.
- One agent reached the 500-step limit: `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8), which failed here. It is also the slowest pair in the other `solo` runs (150 and 336 steps); the median pair took 78 steps.
- Cost `$156.17` (`$1.56` per pair) over 381 minutes, with 24 rate-limit and 4 server-busy retries.
